subject: iq-ai-2025-01 :: BootstrapPool.kill() -> LiquidityManager.moveLiquidity() lifecycle transition
type: cross-contract lifecycle-transition harness (contract A end-state -> transition -> contract B init); clean createPair branch (NOT pair-adoption M-01)
terminal_qualifier: value-safety invariants all hold (no extraction/DoS/conservation break); one runtime CONTROL fact recorded (forced-early migration via gate-donation) that is profit-less, self-funded, and intent-dependent — no severity/exploitability claimed
primary_question: Can attacker-influenced reserve/fee/donation/residual state at kill() materially alter the outcome of moveLiquidity()?
answer: Not in value terms. Across A-E the transition is value-conserving, fee-correct, donation-non-extractable, output-faithful, DoS-free, and boundary price-manipulation arb is a NET LOSS for the attacker. The only attacker-influence on the outcome is TIMING (F): the permissionless moveLiquidity + donation-inflatable gate let an attacker force migration before organic bootstrap by self-funding the full gate threshold (recouping nothing) — a control primitive, not an extraction; harm is intent-dependent.
